public_rationale: Official billing records show movement toward metered usage, including an October enterprise option without included model usage. They also show existing subscriptions remaining available. These changes do not establish that subscriptions have disappeared entirely. Because Zitron supplied no deadline, their persistence through October 28, 2026 does not refute the eventual forecast.
limitations: Supplier-level changes cannot establish a market-wide outcome.
The meaning of subscription matters for access-only fees and hybrid plans.
An unbounded eventual prediction cannot be disproved merely by waiting a finite period.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLM-based subscriptions will go away entirely, at least for code-generating products.

statement.excerpt: I truly believe that LLM-based subscriptions are going to go away entirely, at least at the scale of any product that generates code, and in doing so, Amodei and Altman will wrap up their con, or at least believe that they have.

from_speaker: LLM-based subscriptions are going to go away entirely
at least at the scale of any product that generates code
our_interpretation: The minimum scope is commercially offered LLM products that generate code, including coding assistants.
Subscriptions means recurring paid plans that include some model use. Usage caps, included credits, or metered overages do not by themselves abolish subscriptions.
At least for code-generating products limits the forecast's scope; it is not a conditional antecedent.
No deadline is stated. Continued availability at a finite date does not disprove eventual disappearance.
The accompanying language about a con and the executives' beliefs is not a separate measurable outcome.
criteria.support_condition: Documented completed withdrawal of subscriptions including model use across the commercial LLM coding-product market, with recurring subscription alternatives no longer offered.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Continued subscriptions would contradict a dated disappearance claim, but none was made. Finite persistence alone cannot conclusively contradict this unbounded forecast.
